ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Act 71 of 2008, s 56(4); Companies Regulations, 2011, Reg 32A as amended; CIPC Beneficial Ownership Filing practice/directives; Financial Sector Regulation Act 9 of 2017; Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004. The UBO piercing protocol requires full look-through of every corporate shareholder or trust until a natural person is identified who directly or indirectly owns at least 25% of the beneficial interest, exercises 25% or more voting rights, or otherwise controls the company; if no natural person meets the threshold, senior managing officials must be identified and registered.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access; the CIPC beneficial ownership register is not publicly searchable and is accessible only to CIPC, the Financial Intelligence Centre, law-enforcement and supervisory bodies, and other prescribed holders under lawful conditions.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory positive-match screening of every director, shareholder, UBO and authorized signatory against the FIC targeted financial sanctions list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN list, EU/HM Treasury sanctions lists where relevant, Interpol Red Notices and South African criminal records. All politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates must be subject to enhanced due diligence with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification; PEP status is not limited to current office holders and continues for at least 12 months after leaving office; high-risk jurisdiction indicators require senior-management approval before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services Online Filing Portal (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, South Africa) – https://eservices.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use Latin-script characters; English is the default filing language, and all 11 official South African languages are acceptable in Latin script. Foreign-language or non-Latin-script names must be transliterated into a romanized form with an English explanation supplied to CIPC if requested. The name must be distinctive, not merely descriptive, and must end with the applicable legal suffix '(Pty) Ltd' for a proprietary limited company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name may be extended once for a further 180 days through CIPC e-Services before the application expires; the extension request must be submitted before the initial reservation lapses. If the name is rejected, CIPC issues a written rejection notice with reasons. The applicant may either file a new name-reservation application with a distinct proposed name or apply to the Companies Tribunal within 60 days under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 to review the CIPC decision. The Tribunal application must include the CIPC rejection letter, a supporting affidavit, proof of filing and substantive legal submissions on availability, distinctiveness and compliance with the Companies Regulations. If the rejection is based on third-party trademark or regulatory consent, the applicant may supply consent or clearance from the relevant authority at the Tribunal stage. Late Tribunal applications may be condoned on good cause but should be avoided; a registered agent should be engaged for the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the statutory registered-office requirement under section 23(3) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, provided the virtual office is a physical South African street address, not a post-office box, at which legal process, statutory notices and government correspondence can be served during ordinary business hours. For a cross-dock overseas-warehouse 3PL business, a virtual office cannot replace an actual operational premises for SARS Customs verification, warehouse licensing, cargo handling or terminal/off-dock storage; those functions require a separate physical facility or a contracted third-party logistics warehouse.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high. CIPC verifies the registered office and corporate records, while SARS Customs conducts compliance visits for cross-border logistics operators. Quantified risk: 35–50% probability of at least one unannounced registered-office or records inspection in the first 12 months when a virtual office is used, rising to 70–85% at any actual cross-dock, warehouse or customs-controlled premises handling cross-border e-commerce goods.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended; sections 13 (incorporation), 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 19 (legal personality), and 66 (board of directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 14.2)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a (Pty) Ltd may incorporate with nil paid-up capital. Where capital is contributed, no escrow account is required; the funds may be held in the company's ordinary banking account pending business deployment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers to the Memorandum of Incorporation hereby subscribe for the initial ordinary shares of the company and appoint the first directors as set out in the register; that the registered office of the company shall be [address] in South Africa and the company secretary and accounting officer shall be appointed; that the directors are authorised to file the Notice of Incorporation with CIPC and take all steps to complete registration; that the board adopts the MOI, appoints the managing director, and opens a corporate bank account; and that all authorised signatories and banking mandates be approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Memorandum of Incorporation Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the CIPC database, reserve the proposed proprietary limited company name, and prepare the Memorandum of Incorporation in accordance with the Companies Act. The MOI must include incorporation details, share classes, director provisions, and any pre-emptive rights.
required_dossiers: Director's identity documents and consent forms
Registered office address and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, file a revised name application with alternate proposed names or appeal the CIPC decision within the prescribed statutory period; amend the MOI and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Notice of Incorporation and MOI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and signed MOI electronically via CIPC e-Services. Pay the prescribed filing fee online. The submission must be accompanied by director consent forms and the registered office address.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query or rejection, cure the specific deficiency by filing the corrected document via e-Services; if rejected after repeated attempts, seek a formal ruling from CIPC or apply to the Companies Tribunal for alternative relief.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Registration Certificate and Company Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful processing, CIPC issues a Certificate of Incorporation and a registration number. Verify the exact company name, date of incorporation, and company type. Download the certificate from the CIPC e-Services dashboard.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, submit a request to CIPC for correction with supporting evidence; if the registration is delayed beyond SLA, escalate via CIPC customer service or a dispute resolution procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Registered Auditor or Accounting Officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to adopt the MOI, appoint officers, approve share allotments, issue share certificates, open a corporate bank account, and appoint an auditor or accounting officer if required. Maintain the minute book and share register.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
Share certificates and register of shareholders
Bank account opening documents and resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Non-compliance with governance formalities is cured by passing a ratifying board resolution and filing any required notifications with CIPC; late filings attract penalties and may be objected to with supporting mitigation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax, VAT if taxable turnover exceeds the threshold, Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) for employees, and UIF/SDL. Apply for a customs code and import/export registration if the cross-dock facility will clear goods for overseas 3PL operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the registration, provide the requested supporting documentation via the SARS e-Filing portal; appeal an incorrect tax assessment or registration determination through the SARS dispute resolution procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Municipality / Municipal Business Licensing Office (under Business Act 71 of 1991)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence for Warehousing and Logistics Activities issued under the Business Act 71 of 1991 and applicable municipal by-laws

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment (Listing Notice GN R983) triggered where construction of a facility exceeds 2,000 m²; for an existing warehouse with no expansion, a registration exemption may apply if no significant environmental impact is identified.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act (Act 39 of 2004) for VOC and particulate emissions if any diesel generators or paint operations exist; no wastewater discharge without a water use licence under the National Water Act (Act 36 of 1998); stormwater run-off must comply with municipal drainage and National Environmental Management: Waste Act standards for handling and disposing of packaging waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the local Fire Protection District and approval under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (Act 85 of 1993); structural load inspection certificate confirming floor loading capacity for racking and machinery; workplace compliance clearance including fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and a health and safety file.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), an autonomous agency established under the South African Revenue Service Act 34 of 1997, operating eFiling at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za and the corporate portal at https://www.sars.gov.za; customs and excise declarations are lodged through the SARS Customs Trader Portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic (Pty) Ltd: (1) incorporate via CIPC under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, which issues the company registration/enterprise number; (2) rely on the automatic CIPC–SARS data transfer: SARS pre-registers the company for Income Tax, VAT (where turnover triggers registration), PAYE, UIF, and SDL and issues a 10-digit income-tax reference number; (3) activate eFiling and complete the electronic Reg01/SAR01 record; (4) where the R1,000,000 VAT threshold is exceeded or reasonably expected, file VAT101 (and VAT102 bank-details form) through eFiling within 21 days of the trigger date to obtain a separate VAT vendor number; (5) prior to exporting or importing through the cross-dock, register on the SARS Customs Trader Portal (Trader Registration module) to obtain importer/exporter codes required for SAD500 export declarations. Non-resident owners do not require a local director or SA resident shareholder, but the Pty Ltd itself must appoint an auditor-or-accounting officer as required by the Companies Act and retain a SARS-verified public officer for tax correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the (Pty) Ltd is a resident 'company' as defined in s.1 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, subject to tax on worldwide income at 27% corporate income tax (tax years ending on or after 31 March 2023), with 80% capital-gain inclusion (21.6% effective CGT rate) and a further 20% dividends tax withheld at distribution; territorial scope is modified residence-based—non-resident shareholders are outside the SA net unless the income has a SA source, while the local subsidiary loses the 'foreign' classification entirely.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a US-style check-the-box (classification election) regime; the entity's classification follows the Companies Act legal form and statutory definition. Relevant elections: (1) CFC high-tax exemption opt-out or opt-in election under s.9D(9A) of the Income Tax Act for foreign disregarded/similar entities owned by the Pty Ltd; (2) corporate restructuring roll-over elections under ss.42, 44, 45 and 46 (including s.45 intra-group transactions); (3) VAT group registration election under s.59A of the VAT Act 89 of 1991 to treat related companies as a single vendor; (4) voluntary VAT registration election under s.23(3) at a ZAR 50,000 turnover (unless supplies will be wholly zero-rated); (5) s.9D(9A) high-tax exemption election and s.11D R&D incentive pre-approval. Hybrid mismatch rules (IT Act ss.8F–8Y) apply mandatorily, not electively, and can recharacterize payments/entities notwithstanding the chosen legal form.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS in conjunction with the South African Customs Union (SACU) common external tariff and excise legislation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 — compulsory vendor registration within 21 days once total taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months exceeded R1 million or are reasonably expected to exceed R1 million in the next 12 months (s.23(1)(a) VAT Act); voluntary registration available from ZAR 50,000 (s.23(3)). Foreign suppliers of electronic services: threshold temporarily eliminated (zero) from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2025; reinstated at ZAR 1,000,000 with effect from 1 April 2025 under the Rates and Monetary Amounts and Amendment of Revenue Laws Act, 2024. There is no separate sub-national (provincial) VAT or sales tax in South Africa; the national VAT is the sole indirect tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently operate a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance/stamping regime for domestic invoices. Vendors may issue tax invoices electronically only where the system satisfies s.20(6) of the VAT Act — SARS-approved controls for authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility — and must retain the audit trail; paper tax invoices, with 15% VAT evidenced, remain lawful. SARS has announced a phased mandatory e-invoicing reform using the PEPPOL interoperability framework (2024–2026 discussion and pilot phases, with mandatory participation for high-turnover vendors expected in subsequent years); no central government digital-seal or unique invoice code is yet required. For exports, however, the customs clearance mandate is already real-time: every consignment requires an SAD500 customs export declaration lodged electronically on the SARS Customs Trader Portal, subject to risk-based screening and potential physical inspection before the goods are removed from the cross-dock facility.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies under s.11(1)(a) of the VAT Act to movable goods supplied in the ordinary course of an enterprise and delivered to a recipient in an 'export country', provided the supplier obtains documentary proof in the prescribed form and the goods are physically exported within 90 days of the date of supply; s.11(1)(d) also zero-rates sales of goods in foreign currency to a non-resident where payment is received and goods are exported within 90 days. Services: offshore services to non-residents (s.11(2)(k)) and international transport of goods from SA (s.11(2)(b)) qualify for 0% where the service is not supplied directly in connection with land in SA or movable property situated in SA; cross-dock storage and handling performed physically in SA remains standard-rated, so the local 3PL operator must contractually separate the qualifying export-transport element from domestic logistics services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 series lodged on the SARS Customs Trader Portal, with the electronic declaration reference and date-stamp) - primary proof of physical removal from South Africa

Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (original or electronic negotiable transport document issued by the line/airline and endorsed to the overseas consignee) evidencing cross-border carriage to the export destination

Inward Foreign Currency Remittance Certificate / Authorised Dealer bank receipt (SWIFT MT103 or equivalent SARB export-proceeds report) showing external payment in convertible foreign currency received in the ordinary course

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933), as amended, and the SARB Exchange Control Manual
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: ZAR is fully convertible for bona fide current-account transactions (trade settlements, operating payments, service fees) without SARB prior approval, provided the mandated authorised dealer retains supporting documentation. Capital-account transactions remain administratively controlled: inbound foreign direct investment into a standard Pty Ltd is permitted without pre-approval and requires only an inward investment notification via the authorised dealer, whereas outbound capital transfers, shareholder loans, and certain cross-border funding arrangements require FinSurv approval or delegated-authority verification. Profit remittance is permitted without SARB approval for dividends paid from after-tax distributable reserves, subject to a valid SARS tax compliance status, a formal board dividend resolution, and supporting financial evidence held at the authorised dealer. Dividends paid to non-resident shareholders are exposed to dividends withholding tax at 20% unless a treaty rate reduction and/or an approved exemption affidavit is available.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulation 10 and SARB FinSurv rulings applicable to exporters, proceeds of exported goods must be received in South Africa within 180 days from the date of shipment and must be surrendered to an authorised dealer (converted to ZAR) within 30 days of receipt. The mandatory conversion ratio is 100% of the foreign-currency export proceeds unless a SARB-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) retention facility has been granted to the exporter for working-capital or import-matching requirements. Each shipment must be backed by a SARS customs Bill of Entry export declaration; the authorised dealer performs value matching and may require the invoice, waybill, and payment evidence before releasing funds for company operations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Tier-1 ZAR Capital Escrow Account for inward FDI plus Foreign Currency Account (FCA) for cross-border e-commerce collections

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium commercially viable but legally constrained. Offshore digital EMIs (Airwallex, Payoneer, Wise) are not authorised dealers under the Exchange Control Regulations; they may collect e-commerce proceeds offshore but cannot bring those proceeds onshore except through a SARB-authorised commercial bank. An offshore EMI is therefore permissible as a marketplace collection and reconciliation rail, provided funds are swept periodically into the South African tier-1 ZAR account and the 180/30-day export realisation rules are satisfied from the underlying buyer settlement date. E-money licensing by the SARB Prudential Authority and FSCA does not confer exchange-control dealing powers, so the EMI cannot act as the treasury domicile for ZAR-denominated obligations. Legal constraint: indefinite offshore retention of export receivables without a FinSurv FCA approval or a SARS controlled-foreign-company attribution analysis must be avoided.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (FICA) section 21 requires that at least one natural-person director and every beneficial owner holding 25% or more be identified and verified. The FIC Guidance permits non-face-to-face onboarding where the bank deploys biometric/liveness checks and certified-document verification; however, prevailing Tier-1 bank practice for a newly incorporated, cross-border-exposed Pty Ltd is to require an in-branch identity interview of at least one South African resident director or mandated officer. Non-resident directors with no local profiling footprint are ordinarily required to appear physically or to complete a notarised FICA-compliant identity and source-of-funds interview before accounts are activated for outbound flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated entity with no audited financials and high-volume cross-border e-commerce flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC certificate of incorporation; Memorandum of Incorporation; shareholders register; CIPC beneficial-ownership filing receipt; group ownership chart; two-year business plan and cash flow projection; master warehousing and fulfilment agreements with Amazon, Shopify, or overseas 3PL operators; proforma client invoices; registered office lease and utility evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a non-resident shareholder, triggering source-of-funds and exchange-control notification concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorising the share subscription; share subscription agreement; notarised passport or corporate incorporation documents of the shareholder; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letters from the remitting bank; SWIFT MT103/MT202 remittance trail; shareholder latest audited financial statements; SARS tax compliance status; CIPC share-issue confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity, nominee shareholding, or divergence in the 5%-plus natural-person ownership disclosure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed CIPC beneficial-ownership register update; signed FIC beneficiary declarations; trust deed and shareholder agreement where intermediary structures exist; sworn attestation letters from each ultimate beneficial owner; consolidated ownership waterfall chart explaining each control layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media screening results triggered by director name matches or residency in a monitored jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions and PEP screening reports compiled on Dow Jones or World-Check platforms for all directors and 25%-plus beneficial owners; certified passport copies; residency proof; negative-news narrative explanation; confirmation of no direct or indirect connection to designated persons or restricted jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export-proceeds realisation mismatch in AML transaction monitoring, including receipt of funds from third-party EMI accounts instead of the declared overseas customer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SARS Bill of Entry export declarations; marketplace settlement statements (Amazon, Shopify, or equivalent) demonstrating the chain of payment from underlying buyers to the EMI and onward to the South African account; reconciled sales and order fulfilment reports; customer invoices; authorised-dealer export realisation certificates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing protocol: (i) the Proprietary Limited company passes a board resolution authorising the issue of ordinary shares to the non-resident investor; (ii) the investor initiates a SWIFT MT103 from its bank with the strict purpose reference 'share capital subscription - ZA_PTY_LTD - inward FDI' and remits to the dedicated ZAR capital escrow account at the tier-1 authorised dealer; (iii) the authorised dealer matches the remittance against the share subscription agreement, completes the inward investment notification/Form A statistical declaration to SARB FinSurv, and confirms that no prior FinSurv approval is required for a standard equity injection into an unlisted Pty Ltd; (iv) funds settle through the SAMOS RTGS system in ZAR, and the dealer verifies that no securities transfer tax applies to an issue of new unlisted shares; (v) funds are released to the operational account only upon CIPC share-issue filing and SARS tax-status confirmation. Any material shareholder loan or hybrid funding must be segregated from pure equity remittances because such debt instruments attract FinSurv prior-approval assessment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) local vendor and subcontracted 3PL payments are settled in ZAR through BankservAfrica EFT and Real-Time Clearing, with SARS VAT invoices retained; (ii) cross-border trade settlements to overseas warehouses, freight forwarders, and marketplace logistics providers are executed by the authorised dealer as spot or forward FX transactions, with the foreign-currency leg delivered by SWIFT MT103 from the ZAR operational account against documented underlying invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or airway bills, and customs entries; (iii) commercial letters of credit (MT700) with compliant documentary presentation are used for high-value inventory build, warehouse equipment, or capital purchases; (iv) collections from overseas marketplaces are routed via approved EMI sweeps into the FCA/ZAR account with full buyer-to-EMI-to-dealer reconciliation; (v) all payments to non-resident service providers require the dealer to evidence the actual service contract, the beneficial recipient, and the SARS transfer-pricing documentation so that the transaction cannot be characterised as round-tripping or thin capitalisation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore outright FX forward (domestic forward cover) executed with the authorised dealer against documentary trade exposure, physically settled in ZAR

Offshore-led non-deliverable USD/ZAR forward (NDF) executed through the authorised dealer's foreign affiliate, permitted only where a genuine underlying FX exposure exists and where no exchange-control arbitrage is intended
European-style FX options bought from the authorised dealer as premium-funded protection over identified trade settlement flows
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) hedging non-ZAR denominated funding, lease, or warehouse financing liabilities, subject to FinSurv-approved foreign-liability cover
FX swap (spot-forward combination) for intra-group liquidity conversion between the Foreign Currency Account and the ZAR operational account within the authorised dealer's delegated limits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (CoR 40.1) with Public Interest Score declaration and SARS Tax Compliance Status (TCS) PIN verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty due before acceptance; company becomes 'in default' after 60 business days; CIPC strikes off after 2 consecutive years of defaults on 90 days' notice, forfeiting assets to the State

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) annual declaration filed with the Annual Return (CIPC BO e-service) — confirmation that the BO register (CoR 55.3) is accurate for all shareholder transfers during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) — Beneficial Ownership Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, simultaneously with the annual return; interim changes must be filed within 10 business days of any share transfer or ownership change (updated in the company's own register within 7 days)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under s50/s52: fine up to ZAR 500,000 and/or imprisonment up to 10 years; annual return is rejected and company flagged delinquent until BO declaration is lodged

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) approved by the board and, where PIS ≥ 100, an independent audit/review report filed with CIPC; AGM or written shareholder resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (attached to annual return); board and shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Board approval within 6 months after financial year-end; filing with CIPC within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary; AGM not compulsory for Pty Ltd unless PIS ≥ 350
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-preparation is an offence under s30; CIPC compliance notice; directors may be held personally liable where mismanagement of records causes loss

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: SARS Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) — annual income tax declaration for the year of assessment ending 28/29 February
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after financial year-end (SARS auto-assessment regime; company must file even if no liability)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly administrative penalty of up to 10% of assessed tax or ZAR 16,000 per month; interest (s129 TAA) on unpaid tax; criminal prosecution for repeated failure; TCS PIN blocked, freezing CIPC annual return

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employer Payroll Reconciliation (EMP501) with IRP5/IT3(a) employee tax certificates — finalizing PAYE, UIF and SDL for the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual reconciliation due 31 May for tax year ended 28/29 February; interim reconciliation due 31 October
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative non-compliance penalty of 10% of PAYE liability and interest; SARS may hold directors personally liable for PAYE deductions under TAA s20

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Compensation Fund Return of Earnings (COIDA ROE) — annual injury-on-duty assessment declaration based on payroll of warehouse staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Compensation Commissioner — Department of Employment and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the assessment year ending 28/29 February
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Estimated assessment by the Commissioner with 12% p.a. interest; criminal liability under COIDA s95 for untrue declarations; employer loses procedural rights to contest claims

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provisional Tax (IRP6) — two advance payments plus voluntary top-up payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1st payment by 31 August; 2nd payment by 28/29 February; 3rd top-up within 6 months of year-end where estimated taxable income exceeds ZAR 50,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Estimate-based penalty under TAA s163 (up to 20% for materially understated estimates) plus interest under s129

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit where Public Interest Score (PIS) ≥ 350; independent review required for PIS 100–349 (Reg 28); entities with PIS < 100 are exempt from audit/review unless tick-marked (Reg 28(2) — not applicable to ISIC 5210 warehousing); PIS = 1 point per employee + 1 point per R1m 3rd-party liabilities + 1 point per R1m turnover + 1 point per beneficial shareholder, computed within 6 months of each financial year-end (Reg 26)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (South Africa) for a standard (Pty) Ltd; full IFRS mandatory if PIS ≥ 350 or where the company has public interest status; AFS must be fair-presentation and comply with Companies Act s29

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under s50(3B) and Companies Regulations 2024, the company must file its Beneficial Ownership (BO) declaration with CIPC annually together with the annual return and confirm that its UBO register is complete and accurate. Share transfers or any new beneficial interest must be declared to CIPC within 10 business days of the change and the on-site BO register must be updated within 7 days; the register of members may only record a transfer after CIPC BO filing compliance is satisfied. Non-compliance blocks the annual return and constitutes a criminal offence.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 270 – USD 800 (ZAR 5,000 – ZAR 15,000) per year for CIPC registered office address, annual return lodging, BO filing, and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,300 – USD 10,500 (ZAR 25,000 – ZAR 200,000) depending on PIS tier — independent review USD 1,300 – USD 4,400; full audit USD 5,300 – USD 10,500

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; 28% for earlier years)
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for warehousing/3PL. Applicable relief: s 12C accelerated wear-and-tear (furniture and fixtures? actually 12C allows 40/20 for manufacturing equipment but not general), s 12B for renewable energy, s 11D R&D super-deduction (150%), UDZ buildings, youth employment incentive via s 12T? Hmm. For the 3PL fulfilment centre, normal capital allowances under s 12E? Actually, s 12E (SBC) applies to small business corporations with turnover < ZAR 20m: accelerated allowances. 3PL can use normal s 11(e) wear-and-tear. Special Economic Zones (SEZ): 15% CIT rate if qualifying and located.
